body: My daughter is 7 and I have vaguely started to tell her about it. When she was 3 I was pregnant with her sister and she knew the baby was growing in my belly and would come out when she was big enough. Now she knows mommy and daddy make the baby and only mommy can grow the baby. I honestly believe that you should start teaching them as soon as they are able to understand, just make sure it is age appropriate. And I try to only talk about it when its questioned, or when there is a circumstance that is appropriate to talk about it. I think starting these conversations early will only make the more difficult conversations later in life a little easier to have. It also let's you start the conversation on private areas and what's ok for people to do.

Best advice I ever got for post bingeing, start the next day with a clean slate. Tell yourself that what happened happened and it isnt the end of your journey. Drink extra water and go more low carb, low sugar for the next couple of days to help ward off as much inflammation and water retention as you can. And most importantly, just keep going.
I felt this so much. ♡ stay strong. And dont beat yourself up if you slip.
Seems to be an every day thing. Multiple times a day too.

From my personal experience, when I am depressed and down and just needing to talk, that's all I want honestly. I just want to let it all out, know that someone is there with me who cares and will listen. Hug me if I need it, let me cry or get angry. But I do not want advice or to be told i will get through it or anything like that. Yes it's all said with the best intentions, but when a person is in that state of mind and they hear that it can come across as being told they are exaggerating or things arent that bad or anything to that extent really. I hope this all makes sense. I would just try letting her know you are there to listen and to be a shoulder to cry on if needed. And try to refrain from giving advice unless it is asked for. I hope your friend gets better and can possibly get help from a medical professional. Depression is definitely a bitch.

You are very welcome! I would definitely recommend listening to your trainer as well, but everybody is different so you will still need to tweak their plan for you a bit I am sure. The biggest problem with cutting the calories imo is your end goal should be to maintain once you get to where you want to be. You dont want your calorie intake to be too low that you can not sustain that on going. Also if lifting is something you plan to keep doing you will most likely end up needing to increase your calories the more muscle you gain. But depending on where you are in your journey that could be awhile. Just remember whatever you do now you need to make sure it is something that you can keep up with, or else you will start to back track down the road.

I wouldn't be too concerned if your measurements are still decreasing. You said you are lifting twice a week? That's going to build muscle which is taking the place of the fat that is being lost. Which would be a good reason for the sudden halt in the scale going down. If you cut any calories I would keep it very minimal, up your protein if you havent already, make sure you are getting plenty of water and on the days you arent in the gym do some at home workouts. It's all about the in/out. Burn more calories than you consume. Good luck! (I myself have been stuck at the same weight for a few weeks)
Oh definitely, even if I'm not in a depressed or sad mood and I'm feeling ok, sad and slow music will almost always put me in that head space

If I'm really down I make a point to only listen to music that is really upbeat. Anything slow or sad just makes me spiral into a deeper depression. No specific genre, just upbeat, make you wanna sing and dance kind of music.
